# LC-GRPO: Bridging Train-Inference Gap for Flow-Based GRPO with Langevin Correction

- **Authors**: Yingqing Guo, Hui Yuan, Zijian He, Mengdi Wang, Zheng Ding
- **Venue**: cs.LG
- **Published**: 2026-08-06
- **Source**: arxiv
- **Link**: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05600>
- **PDF**: <https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.05600v1>
- **Topics**: reasoning-training
- **Relevance score**: reasoning-training 0.50

## In one line

A GRPO variant for flow-based generative models that replaces SDE training rollouts with an ODE step plus a Langevin correction, aligning training samples with the deterministic sampler used at test time.

## Problem

Flow-based generative models are sampled by solving a deterministic ODE, while online RL needs stochastic rollouts to explore. Existing flow GRPO methods swap the ODE for an SDE during training. The two share marginals in continuous time but their finite-step discretizations differ substantially, and SDE rollouts blur as exploration noise rises, so the samples optimized are not the samples the test-time sampler produces.

## Contributions

- LC-GRPO: an inference-aligned ODE Euler step followed by a Langevin correction as the RL rollout transition for flow models
- Recovery of the required score from the flow velocity, needing no additional score model
- A proof that one Langevin correction reduces the Wasserstein error of an imperfect ODE Euler step
- A comparison showing the proposed transition can beat Euler-Maruyama discretization at matched randomness
- Results on SD3.5-Medium, FLUX.1-Dev and HunyuanVideo across text-to-image and text-to-video

## Method

Each rollout transition first takes an inference-aligned ODE Euler step, then applies a stochastic Langevin correction targeting the marginal at the resulting timestep. The score needed for the correction is recovered directly from the flow velocity, so no separate score model is required, and the resulting transition stays an isotropic Gaussian with a tractable likelihood usable for policy optimization. The paper proves that under suitable conditions one Langevin correction step reduces the Wasserstein error of an imperfect ODE Euler step, and that at a matched randomness level the proposed transition can be more accurate than standard Euler-Maruyama discretization of the reverse SDE.

## Results

On SD3.5-Medium, FLUX.1-Dev and HunyuanVideo, LC-GRPO consistently improves reward optimization on text-to-image and text-to-video tasks, preserves generation quality, and narrows the gap between stochastic training rollouts and deterministic test-time ODE inference. No numbers are given in the abstract.

## Limitations

No quantitative results in the abstract. The theoretical guarantees hold 'under suitable conditions' and at a matched randomness level, neither specified here. Evaluation is on image and video generation only; nothing is reported for language models or reasoning. Reward optimization in this setting is measured against learned reward models, whose gaming is a known failure mode not addressed.

## Why it matters here

- **reasoning-training**: Off-target for reasoning: the models are image and video generators and no language or reasoning benchmark appears. It matched this topic on the token GRPO alone. The one idea worth carrying over is the framing — that RL exploration noise injected during training changes the distribution the policy is optimized on relative to the deterministic decoder used at test time. Language RLVR has the same structure, since rollouts are sampled at temperature and evaluation is often greedy, and the archive holds no paper that measures that gap directly.

## Abstract

Flow-based generative models are typically sampled by solving a deterministic ordinary differential equation (ODE), whereas online reinforcement learning requires stochastic rollouts for policy exploration and optimization. Existing GRPO methods for flow models therefore replace the inference-time ODE with a stochastic differential equation (SDE) during training. Although the ODE and SDE share the same marginal distributions in continuous time, their finite-step discretizations can differ substantially. In particular, SDE rollouts often become blurry as the exploration noise increases, creating a mismatch between the samples used for reinforcement learning and those generated by the test-time ODE sampler. We introduce LC-GRPO, a flow-based GRPO framework with Langevin correction. Each rollout transition first takes an inference-aligned ODE Euler step and then applies a stochastic Langevin correction targeting the marginal distribution at the resulting timestep. The required score is recovered directly from the flow velocity, requiring no additional score model, while the resulting transition remains an isotropic Gaussian with a tractable likelihood for policy optimization. We theoretically show that, under suitable conditions, one Langevin correction step reduces the Wasserstein error of an imperfect ODE Euler step. At a matched randomness level, we further show that the proposed transition can be more accurate than the standard Euler--Maruyama discretization of the reverse SDE. Experiments on SD3.5-Medium, FLUX.1-Dev, and HunyuanVideo demonstrate that LC-GRPO consistently improves reward optimization across text-to-image and text-to-video tasks, preserves generation quality, and substantially narrows the gap between stochastic training rollouts and deterministic test-time ODE inference.
